status: frozen 2026-11-03 before any re-test or re-merge of published runs
question: On the GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 coop runs behind the CooperBench paper, how many runs that fail the paper's merge pipeline pass after our llm re-merge, and how much of the coop-solo gap does that close?
decision_rule: Calibration first: on a random sample of clean-merge pairs per model, our harness must reproduce the paper's recorded per-feature test results on at least 90% of features; if it does not, results are reported with that caveat. Primary, per model: coop success with our llm re-merge added after the paper's pipeline, against the paper's recorded coop success on the same pairs (95% bootstrap CI clustered by task). The claim that much of the coop-solo gap is a merge artifact holds for a model if the re-merge closes at least a third of that model's gap (recorded solo minus recorded coop, on pairs with both) and the CI of the gain is above 0.

source.paper_pipeline: git merge-file, then a union merge, then a small learned resolver (paper Sec. 2.2 and App. B); recorded per pair as naive, union and llm results in aggregated_results_<model>_k1.json

exclude_note: firecrawl is in the published runs but not in the pinned CooperBench dataset, so its tests cannot be run

calibration.rule: pairs whose naive merge was clean and whose per-feature results were recorded

remerge.rule: pairs whose naive merge conflicted and that fail every stage of the paper's pipeline

own.rule: the remerge pairs; each agent's own patch is tested alone
own.note: post hoc, added 2026-11-03 after the primary result: separates conflicted pairs where both agents' own work passes (integration cases) from pairs with a feature that fails anyway, to tell whether the re-merge falls short or integration cases are rare
